scenario_titles.a: badge readable, hidden while the worker stays in view, readable again
scenario_titles.b: occlusion and re-entry (60 frames away) with the badge hidden, readable later
scenario_titles.c: two workers in identical PPE walk past each other soon after entering; badges hidden in random segments (independently per worker, about half the frames)
scenario_titles.d: one badge never readable, alongside a badge-identified worker in identical PPE
scenario_titles.b_close: as b, but the worker leaves again before the badge is read on the re-entry track; that fragment can only be folded at end-of-session consolidation
scenario_titles.c_named: control (first design of c): badges hidden i.i.d. per frame, both workers named before the crossing
scenario_titles.c_persp: as c, with the worker further back drawn 300 px tall (consistent perspective)
scenario_titles.d_noreturn: as d, but the badge-identified worker leaves and does not return

meta.harness: real SafetyPipeline (phase2/src/pipeline.py) with src.detector.Detector replaced in-process by a stub returning ground-truth Person (3) and No-Helmet (1) boxes at confidence 0.9 (full-extent boxes; class-wise NMS at IoU 0.7 emulated); per-frame state captured by wrapping instance methods; pipe.close() at the end

definitions.time_to_named_s: first frame whose IdentityResult label equals the worker's configured name, minus the frame the worker first appears, / 30. Includes ByteTrack's 1-frame activation lag. A name obtained by appearance/position matching counts.
definitions.time_to_first_badge_read_s: first frame in which the worker's OWN marker is decoded and assigned to the worker's own ByteTrack id by WorkIdBinder._assign (captured), minus the first-appearance frame, / 30. 'in_badge_of' (tid in badge_of) is also logged per frame; it includes sticky labels.
definitions.wrong_name: a person-frame whose IdentityResult label is ANOTHER worker's configured name; an event is a maximal stretch of that worker's identity outputs on one ByteTrack id that all carry the same wrong label (frames with no identity output for the worker -- box withheld by the NMS emulation, probation -- neither end nor extend it).
definitions.false_merge: reid_eval._score on (true worker, uid) per identified person-frame, frame order then worker order: an assignment whose (remapped) uid is already owned by a different true worker (the first logged owns it); rate = false merges / all assignments. live = uids as output; consolidated = _remap_from(consolidation merges) [paper's +offline]; final = _remap_from(live take_merges + consolidation merges) [the records the report ends with].
definitions.anonymous_record: a uid first output with an anonymous 'Worker N' label. Only its ANONYMOUS period is attributed to it: the person-frames output under it while the label was 'Worker N' (frames, owner = majority true worker of those) and the violation episodes opened while it was anonymous. Kinds: 'fragment' = a SECOND record of a worker whose badge is read in the run (the worker already had a uid when it was created, e.g. a re-entry with the badge hidden); 'initial_anonymous' = the worker's FIRST record, created because the badge was hidden when the track was committed, renamed in place when the badge is read; 'anonymous_identity' = a record of a worker whose badge is never read (d, d_noreturn).
definitions.at_reacquisition: renamed in place (same uid now carries a configured name) or merged live (take_merges during process) -- correct if into the owner's name; 'episodes_in_named_record_at_reacquisition' checks the WorkerHistory record holding each of the record's anonymous-period episodes right after that frame; 'episodes_open_at_reacquisition' = those still open then.
definitions.at_end_of_session: after pipe.close() (consolidation + history.close): the label of the record that holds the anonymous record (live + consolidation merges followed).
definitions.wrong_merge: kind 'assignment': a worker's person-frames given a uid first logged for another worker; kind 'live_merge'/'consolidation_merge': a merge of two uids first logged for different workers. misattributed_worker's data (from_uid) went into into_uid, owned by into_owner. forward_corrected_frame = a later frame of that worker under a uid it owns (the identity layer stops misattributing; NOT an undo). final_record_workers = the true workers whose person-frames end in that final record; still_merged_at_end = both the misattributed worker and the owner are among them (i.e. not undone).
definitions.undo_invariants: checked every frame: a WorkerHistory record's frames_seen never decreases; an IdentityManager worker's frames_seen never decreases; a uid merged away live is never output again; an episode changes record only along a merge made in that frame, and never returns to a record it left.
definitions.binder: binder_misassigned_reads = person-frames whose track was assigned ANOTHER worker's marker this frame (to_smaller_box: the receiving box had a strictly smaller area than the badge owner's box -- workid._assign gives a tag inside two boxes to the smaller one); binder_wrong_bindings = distinct (worker, ByteTrack id, wrong name) binder labels, i.e. tracks the binder bound to another worker's name; own_badge_decoded_but_not_bound_to_own_track = the worker's marker was decoded somewhere in the frame but not assigned to its track: on a (re-)entering worker's first frame ByteTrack outputs no id yet, while two boxes contain the tag the binder's 'too close to call' rule refuses, or the tag went to the other (smaller) box.
definitions.record_owner: a record whose label is a configured name belongs to that name's worker; an anonymous record to the majority true worker of the assignments that end in it.
definitions.oracle_boxes: Person boxes are the full (amodal) extent of each rendered figure, as painted (int() rounding: 134 or 135 px wide at 320 px, varying per frame); class-wise NMS at IoU 0.7 is emulated (the deployed detector's ultralytics default), keeping the less-occluded box.

caveats.crossings: Binder outcomes while two boxes overlap depend on the oracle geometry: (1) boxes are full-extent (amodal), so the back worker's box can cover the front worker's badge; a real detector's box for a half-hidden person may be tighter; (2) workid._assign gives a tag that lies inside two boxes to the SMALLER box (refusing only if the areas are within 5 % AND the containments within 0.05). In c / c_named both figures are 320 px, so which box is smaller is decided by a 1 px int() rounding of the rendered width (random per frame); c_persp draws the back worker 6 % smaller, as consistent perspective would, so his box is always smaller. Treat binder mis-assignments in the crossings as conditional on amodal boxes.
caveats.c_named: In c_named both tracks get a sticky badge binding within a few frames of entering, long before the crossing, and ByteTrack keeps both ids through it, so the per-frame hiding cannot change any identity output there: its result is fixed before the crossing starts.
caveats.oracle_tracking: Oracle boxes move smoothly (sway + constant-speed walk) and are never missed except by the NMS emulation, so ByteTrack's Kalman prediction bridges the crossings easily; a real detector's jitter and misses could cause id switches the oracle does not. Whether any ByteTrack id ever covered both workers is reported per scenario (info.bytetrack_ids_covering_two_workers).
